answer: Plume-weighted coordination pricing. Each identity carries a plume score fixed at first action: an escalating fee equal to the harmonic sum of every concurrent action it joins in a window. Concurrent actions emit an echo tag, and any two identities sharing echo tags above a threshold have their fees multiplied by the overlap count. A velvet flood of cheap clones thus pays superlinear aggregate fees, since each clone's marginal action raises every sibling's price. Defending one sock puppet costs the attacker the full sibling fee surface, not a flat bond.
